2G|001011.Description: Number of requests for TCHs that are rejected because there are no radio resources available. All kinds of procedures used to request a TCH are considered, that is, the TCH is rejected if there is no requested resources available for assignments using the normal TCH assignment procedure and assignments for all kinds of (incoming) handovers. This counter is also updated when a request for TCH is rejected because of a mismatch between the types of the requested channel and the A interface circuit.  See also counter 004079.

This counter is also updated when a request for TCH is rejected because of a mismatch between the types of the requested channel and the A interface circuit.  See also counter 004079.
2G|001011.Updated: When the RRM has no TCHs available for either call or HO attempt requests, or the RRM changes the A interface circuit pool before the TCH allocation. This counter may be updated immediately after a TCH request or, in case of queuing,when the queuing timer expires. NOTE! In case of DR this counter is updated as follows: 1) When a call is removed from the queue because of a DR attempt, this counter is NOT updated on the SOURCE side, instead counter 001173 is updated. 2) If queuing is not used or the queuing timer expires before a DR attempt, this counter is updated on the SOURCE side. 3) On the TARGET side, this counter is updated in case of congestion (blocking). 2G|001155.Updated: When the SDCCH channel allocation does not succeed because of a lack of SDCCH resources at the time of the immediate assignment. When SDCCH is released with the dx-cause rtsl_reconf_fail_c.   Triggered for example when a dynamic SDCCH allocation (1154 DYNAMIC_SDCCH_RECONFIGURATION_ATTEMPT) is tried but it fails. Failure can be caused for example by the following situations.   - In the BCSU/BCXU there cannot be more SDCCH allocated.  - All TCHs are busy and cannot be reallocated.  - RRM has reconfigured a TCH to SDCCH but ABI cannot do the same. In this case the dynamic SDCCH seized by RRM is released with cause rtsl_reconf_fail and the call attempt fails (blocking).   See figure FACCH call setup because of SDCCH congestion with counters.

2G|001174.Description: Number of territory upgrade requests received from the Packet Controller Unit.
2G|001174.Description in previous release: Number of territory upgrade requests received from the Packet Controller Unit.
2G|001174.Updated: "When the Radio Resource Management receives from the Packet Controller Unit a request for new radio time slots to be added into the GPRS territory. The PCU can request an upgrade after BSC has fulfilled the default territory defined by the operator parameters.  The upgrade of the GPRS territory may be started for various reasons, for example when GPRS is set enabled in a BTS, GPRS-TRX is created or deblocked, TSL inside the GPRS territory is deblocked or CS load decreases, but this counter is not triggered in these cases.  This counter is triggered only when GPRS Territory Upgrade is started by Packet Switched Radio Resource Management requesting additional GPRS capacity.  Incase of DLDC territory upgrade request, this counter is updated together with counter 001257 - GPRS TERRITORY UPGRADE REQUEST DUE DLDC"

2G|001216.Updated: When there is no BCSU/BCXU capacity available for either call or HO attempt requests. This counter may be updated either immediately after a TCH request or, in case of queuing, when the queuing timer expires.  When the TCH request is rejected in case of directed retry (DR), this counter is updated as follows:  1) When a call is removed from the queue due to a DR attempt, this counter is NOT updated on the SOURCE side. Instead, counter 001173 is updated.  2) If queuing is not used or the queuing timer expires before a DR attempt, this counter is updated on the SOURCE side.  3) On the TARGET side, this counter is updated in case of congestion (blocking).

2G|003014.Description: Average number of busy RACHs on a CCCH.  Counter 003015 is updated along with this counter.
2G|003014.Description in previous release: Average number of busy RACHs on a CCCH.  Counter 003015 is updated along with this counter.
2G|003014.Updated: When the value of the RACH load is received in a CCCH_LOAD_INDICATION message from the BTS during a measurement period. The number of busy RACHs is added to the previous value and the number of the events is increased by one.  NOTE! This RACH counter is triggered when the RX Level is above -100dBm. Other detection methods (like CRC or S/N) are not applied. This means that high load on RACH may occure even without a significant number of CHANNEL_REQUIRED messages. For example, RACHs from different MSs can clash and cause a high signal level, but the decoding does not find any detectable RACH. The interference causes lots of bursts that trigger the counter, but these bursts are then filtered out in the detection.  See figure CCCH load indication.

2G|003036.Description: The sum of the average paging buffer occupancy percentages. Each time a CCCH load reporting period ends, the occupancy percentage is calculated and reported in a CCCH LOAD INDICATION message. The average is calculated with (100*N)/N(max)%, where N is the occupied buffer space and N(max) is the maximum buffer space during the CCCH load reporting period.   The CCCH load reporting period is the time between CCCH LOAD INDICATION message sendings. This counter stores the sum of the average paging buffer values received in CCCH LOAD INDICATION messages.   Counter 003037 is updated along with this counter.

2G|003060.Description: Number of deleted RACH (Channel Required messages) in BSC when BTS is protected against overload.
2G|003060.Description in previous release: Number of deleted RACH (Channel Required messages) in BSC when BTS is protected against overload.
2G|003060.Updated: When new RACH is deleted in BSC due to overload in BTS. RACH gets deleted in BSC when maximum number of currently allowed simultaneous CS call setups in the BTS is exceeded; therefore new call setup cannot be started at the moment. The BTS may ask BSC to lower the number of simultaneous CS call setups temporary due to high load in the BCF. The BSC accordingly limits new call setups in all segments in the BCF. The BTS informs BSC when there is no more need to limit CS call setups. By default maximum number of simultaneous CS call setups in a cell/segment depends on the CCCH TRXSIG and CCCH channel configuration.

When DL Rx level is low, there is a risk that another Radio Access Network causes interference to GSM system.

2G|005006.Description: Sum of TRX specific downlink RF power level value samples in the serving cell. The value range of a single RF power level sample is 0...15.   RF power level value mapping (Pmax is the maximum transmission power of the BTS):  0 -> Pmax - 0 dBm  1 -> Pmax - 2 dBm  2 -> Pmax - 4 dBm  ...  15 -> Pmax - 30 dBm.   If Pmax is 43 dBm, then the value 0 means 43 dBm and the value 15 means 13 dBm.   The average TRX specific downlink RF power level used in the cell can be calculated by dividing this counter with the denominator counter 005007 POWER DENOMINATOR 2.

2G|005034.Description: Sum of the TRX specific SAIC capable MS related downlink RF power level value samples in the serving cell. The RF power level value samples are taken from every 40th MS report received by the BSC during a call. The value range of a single RF power level sample is 0..15.    RF power level value mapping (Pmax is the maximum transmission power of the BTS): 0 -> Pmax - 0 dBm  1 -> Pmax - 2 dBm  2 -> Pmax - 4 dBm ...  15 -> Pmax - 30 dBm.  If Pmax is 43 dBm, then the value 0 means 43 dBm and the value 15 means 13 dBm.  The average TRX specific downlink RF power level used in the cell can be calculated by dividing this counter with the denominator counter 005035 AVERAGE SAIC BS POWER DENOMINATOR.

On fast link adaptation (LA) mode the codec mode is the last codec mode used during the radio link measurement interval. 2G|015007.Updated: Updated once during a measurement period according to 3GPP 24.008 based on the adjacent cell LAC/CI pair information of an internal inter-cell or an external handover request. When the PLMN and the LAC of the adjacent cell are missing, the LAC information of this counter is set to 0xFFFE, and the corresponding counter 015238 PLMN ID 1 is set to 0x999999.  See figures:  - Successful internal inter-cell SDCCH or TCH handover  - Unsuccessful internal inter-cell SDCCH or TCH handover due to lack of resources  - Successful external SDCCH or TCH handover, source BSC  - Successful external SDCCH or TCH handover, target BSC  - Unsuccessful external SDCCH or TCH handover due to lack of resources, source BSC. In this case the counter HO fail res to adj x, which is the first cell of the HO_REQUIRED message, is updated.  - Unsuccessful external SDCCH or TCH handover due to lack of resources, target BSC  - Successful external handover with successful queueing, target BSC  - Unsuccessful external SDCCH or TCH handover, source BSC. The GSM timer T7 expires in the BSC.  - Internal directed retry  - External directed retry, source BSC  - External directed retry, target BSC

2G|052003.Updated: On a regular TRX: - when the RRM receives a TCH request either in a call or HO attempt  NOTE! A BTS can have more than one regular TRX, but this counter is updated merely on one regular TRX of the BTS.  On a super-reuse TRX: This counter increases by one when the Radio Resource Management receives a TCH request either in a call (underlay - overlay assignment or direct access) or in a handover attempt to a super-reuse TRX, and the TRX in question is one of the candidates in the target TRX list.  NOTE! This counter is updated on every super-reuse TRX which is on the target TRX list in an HO attempt to a super-reuse TRX.  The counter update is visible in all figures of 52 Underlay-Overlay Statistics Measurement except for the following: - Counters are updated every 20 seconds - Unsuccessful internal intra-cell underlay-overlay handover from regular to super-reuse TRX - Unsuccessful internal intra-cell underlay-overlay handover from super-reuse to regular TRX - Unsuccessful internal intra-cell underlay-overlay handover within super TRXs - Unsuccessful internal inter-cell underlay-overlay handover from parent to child cell - Unsuccessful internal inter-cell underlay-overlay handover from child to parent cell - Unsuccessful internal intra-cell underlay-overlay handover attempt due to bad quality experience on the super-reuse frequency or unallowed handover because estimated C/I ratio is too low - Successful internal intra-cell frequency type (FRT) underlay-overlay handover from super-reuse to the super-reuse TRX - Unsuccessful internal intra-cell frequency type underlay-overlay handover from super-reuse to the super-reuse TRX due to connection failure on the new channel, MS returns to the old channel

2G|072027.Description: The number of successful uplink TBF reallocations.
2G|072027.Description in previous release: The number of successful uplink TBF reallocations.
2G|072027.Updated: When new resources are allocated for an uplink TBF, for example, when the number of TSLs for an existing TBF is changed. A TBF receives a new TFI when, and only when, it is reallocated. The reallocation is detected from the changed TFI, that is, neither the channels that are used, nor their number does necessarily have to change in reallocation.   Other possible reasons for reallocation include, for example:  - territory downgrades (CSW traffic) - the establishment of simultaneous TBFs to downlink - the availability of better resources on other channels - a change of requirements from the MS.  The PCU can change the uplink TCH configuration at any time by sending the MS a PACKET_UPLINK_ASSIGNMENT or a PACKET_TIMESLOT_RECONFIGURE message. If the reallocation is impossible, for example, in a GPRS territory downgrade, the PCU can release a TBF with a PDCH_RELEASE message.   This counter is updated separately for normal, extended and super-extended areas.

If either of them is received before T3169 expiration, a corresponding counter 072058 UL TBF REL DUE TO FLUSH or 072060 UL TBF REL DUE TO SUSPEND is updated instead.   This counter is updated separately for normal, extended and super-extended areas. This counter is not updated when UL TBF is in extended mode.

2G|072062.Description: The number of valid RLC data blocks in uplink with CS1.
2G|072062.Description in previous release: The number of valid RLC data blocks in uplink with CS1.
2G|072062.Updated: When the RLC receives a valid, new uplink RLC data block with CS1 coding scheme. This counter does not include retransmissions, but it is triggered both in acknowledged and unacknowledged modes. The MS is told with either the IMMEDIATE_ASSIGNMENT or the PACKET_UPLINK_ASSIGNMENT message which CS to use initially in the uplink data transfer. The PCU can command the MS to change the CS by sending a PACKET_UPLINK_ACK/NACK message that includes a Channel Coding Command field. In retransmissions the same CS has to be used as in the initial block transmission.   This counter is updated separately for normal, extended and super-extended areas.
2G|072062.Updated in previous release: When the RLC receives a valid, new uplink RLC data block with CS1 coding scheme. This counter does not include retransmissions, but it is triggered both in acknowledged and unacknowledged modes. The PCU can command the MS to change the CS by sending a PACKET_UPLINK_ACK/NACK message that includes a Channel Coding Command field. In retransmissions the same CS has to be used as in the initial block transmission.   This counter is updated separately for normal, extended and super-extended areas.

2G|072063.Description: The number of new RLC data blocks in downlink with CS1. This counter does not count the retransmitted data blocks.
2G|072063.Description in previous release: The number of new RLC data blocks in downlink with CS1. This counter does not count the retransmitted data blocks.
2G|072063.Updated: When a valid, new RLC data block is sent in downlink with CS1 coding scheme. This counter does not include retransmissions, but is triggered both in acknowledged and unacknowledged modes. In downlink data transfer the PCU selects the CS to be used, and the code word for the selected CS is included in each sent RLC data block. If the CS is changed during one TBF reservation, the new CS code word is included in the blocks. In retransmissions the same CS has to be used as in the initial block transmission. Note that unacknowledged RLC blocks always use CS1 and trigger this counter.  This counter is updated separately for normal, extended and super-extended areas..
2G|072063.Updated in previous release: When a valid, new RLC data block is sent in downlink with CS1 coding scheme. This counter does not include retransmissions, but is triggered both in acknowledged and unacknowledged modes. In downlink data transfer the PCU selects the CS to be used, and the code word for the selected CS is included in each sent RLC data block. If the CS is changed during one TBF reservation, the new CS code word is included in the blocks. In retransmissions the same CS has to be used as in the initial block transmission. Note that unacknowledged RLC blocks always use CS1 and trigger this counter.  This counter is updated separately for normal, extended and super-extended areas..
2G|072063.Counter Description: The number of new RLC data blocks in downlink with CS1. This counter does not count the retransmitted data blocks.

2G|072074.Description in previous release: The number of uplink TBF establishment requests during a downlink TBF.
2G|072074.Updated: When an uplink TBF is requested during a downlink TBF. The MS can request resources for an uplink TBF by including a Channel Request Description IE in the PACKET_DOWNLINK_ACK/NACK message. If there is no need to change the downlink TCH configuration, the PACKET_DOWNLINK_ASSIGNMENT message is used to tell the uplink TCH configuration and USF values of each TCH and TFI to the MS. If the downlink TCH configuration is changed, a PACKET_TIMESLOT_RECONFIGURE message is used to tell the MS both the uplink and downlink TCH configuration and USF values of the uplink TCHs as well as the uplink and downlink TFIs. The procedure is complete when the first block on the assigned uplink TCH is received. This procedure is guarded by a timer. If the PACKET_UPLINK_ASSIGNMENT fails, the uplink TBF is released. If the PACKET_TIMESLOT_RECONFIGURE fails, both the downlink and uplink TBFs are released.
2G|072074.Updated in previous release: When an uplink TBF is requested during a downlink TBF. If the downlink TCH configuration is changed, a PACKET_TIMESLOT_RECONFIGURE message is used to tell the MS both the uplink and downlink TCH configuration and USF values of the uplink TCHs as well as the uplink and downlink TFIs. The procedure is complete when the first block on the assigned uplink TCH is received. This procedure is guarded by a timer. If the PACKET_UPLINK_ASSIGNMENT fails, the uplink TBF is released. 2G|072109.Network Element Name: VOLUME WEIGHTED LLC THROUGHPUT EDGE 4 DL NUMERATOR
2G|072109.Network Element Name in previous release: VOLUME WEIGHTED LLC THROUGHPUT EDGE 4 DL NUMERATOR
2G|072109.Description: The numerator for downlink Volume Weighted (VW) LLC throughput in EDGE mode, for MSs which are capable of four or more TSLs in downlink allocation. Longer data bursts are weighted more than short bursts. The counter contains the sum of the throughputs weighted by the volume of each LLC transmission burst within the TBF. An LLC transmission burst is a transmission period between two transmission breaks. The unit of the counter is 100 bytes^2/10 ms. Average VW throughput in EDGE mode is achieved by dividing 072109 by 072110.   In DTM mode this counter is updated if the DTM multi-slot class allows to allocate four or more TSLs for the DTM PS connection.  Counter 072110 is updated along with this counter.

2G|072201.Description in previous release: The number of cases where an ongoing UL TBF needs to be released due to a DTM procedure.
2G|072201.Updated: The PCU increases this counter when a UL TBF is released due to one of the following reasons: - PCU receives from the DX a request to release an ongoing DTM call. - PCU receives from the DX a request to establish a DTM allocation for an MS having a UL TBF in GPRS mode. - PCU receives an indication that an MS having a UL TBF in GPRS mode has entered dedicated mode.  This counter also registers events triggered by DTM reallocations to the extended area. All events are registered under the normal area object.  This counter is not updated for PCU1. 2G|090015.Updated: This counter is updated whenever PCU starts the QoS based AC procedure at TBF establishment.  In DL direction the QoS based AC procedure is started when a new DL TBF needs to be established and when the DL-UNITDATA PDU has the T-bit value of 1 (it indicates that the PDU carries user data and not GMM/SM signaling).  In UL direction the QoS based AC procedure is started when  a) One-phase access: MS sends EGPRS PACKET CHANNEL REQUEST message with access type = 'One Phase Access Request' and with Radio Priority larger than zero.  b) Two-phase access: MS sends PACKET RESOURCE REQUEST message with access type = 'Two Phase Access Request' and with Radio Priority larger than zero.  c) DTM request: MS sends DTM REQUEST message with Packet Establishment Cause = User data and with Radio Priority field larger than zero.
2G|090015.Updated in previous release: This counter is updated whenever PCU starts the QoS based AC procedure at TBF establishment.  In DL direction the QoS based AC procedure is started when a new DL TBF needs to be established and when the DL-UNITDATA PDU has the T-bit value of 1 (it indicates that the PDU carries user data and not GMM/SM signaling).  In UL direction the QoS based AC procedure is started when  a) One-phase access: MS sends EGPRS PACKET CHANNEL REQUEST message with access type = 'One Phase Access Request' and with Radio Priority larger than zero.  b) Two-phase access: MS sends PACKET RESOURCE REQUEST message with access type = 'Two Phase Access Request' and with Radio Priority larger than zero.  c) DTM request: MS sends DTM REQUEST message with Packet Establishment Cause = User data and with Radio Priority field larger than zero.
2G|090015.Counter Description: Number of times the QoS based Admission Control check is done at TBF establishment.

2G|090016.Description: Number of times a TBF establishment is rejected due to the QoS based Admission Control procedure.
2G|090016.Description in previous release: Number of times a TBF establishment is rejected due to the QoS based Admission Control procedure.
2G|090016.Updated: This counter is updated whenever the QoS based AC fails due to the fact that the capacity that the TBF would get per timeslot is less than a given parameter threshold value. Note: The capacity is shared among the users with respect to their weights. Therefore, a high priority user (ARP = 1) gets a larger share from the timeslot capacity than a low priority user (ARP = 3) and hence a low priority user is more likely rejected by the QoS based AC than a high priority user.
2G|090016.Updated in previous release: This counter is updated whenever the QoS based AC fails due to the fact that the capacity that the TBF would get per timeslot is less than a given parameter threshold value. Note: The capacity is shared among the users with respect to their weights. Therefore, a high priority user (ARP = 1) gets a larger share from the timeslot capacity than a low priority user (ARP = 3) and hence a low priority user is more likely rejected by the QoS based AC than a high priority user.
2G|090016.Counter Description: Number of times a TBF establishment is rejected due to the QoS based Admission Control procedure.

2G|099002.Description: A sum of the signals of adjacent cells for each serving cell over the measurement period.  TOTAL_INTERFERENCE = TOTAL_INTERFERENCE - 1 + [ dBm2W(I1)+dBm2W(I2)+...+dBm2W(I6) ] / dBm2W[ max(I1,I2,I3,I4,I5,I6) ]  where: - dBm2W is a mapping from dBm to mW*10-12 - I1, I2, I6 are RXLevels (-110 dBm  -47 dBm) of adjacent cells  In case of overflow in the BCSU/BCXU, the value of this counter is set to FFFF FFFE. In case of an overflow in the OMU, the value is set to FFFF FFFF.

2G|104000.Network Element Name: IBHO ATT TO UTRAN DEFAULT ANE
2G|104000.Network Element Name in previous release: IBHO ATT TO UTRAN DEFAULT ANE
2G|104000.Description: The number of IMSI-based handover attempts from the GSM to the default authorised network because of coverage of UTRAN cell of an equivalent PLMN.  The default authorised network is used for an unidentified subscriber. This means that the corresponding subscriber group could not find the subscriber.  Failure of the attempts can be seen in the counter IBHO UNS TO UTRAN DEFAULT ANE of the IBHO measurement. Corresponding handover counters in HO measurement are updated normally in addition to this counter.

2G|123015.Description: Number of downlink RTP packets, containing TRAU frames of circuit switched U-plane, lost based on missing sequence number. This counter does not include those received too early or late.
2G|123015.Description in previous release: Number of downlink RTP packets, containing TRAU frames of circuit switched U-plane, lost based on missing sequence number. This counter does not include those received too early or late.
2G|123015.Updated: When the next sequence number is missing from downlink RTP packet containing TRAU frames of circuit switched U-plane. If the gap in the RTP sequence numbers is less than a given threshold value (100), then the counter is incremented by the amount of missing RTP packets. If the gap in the RTP sequence numbers is larger than or equal to the threshold value (100), then it is interpreted that there is a jump in the RTP sequence numbers (might happen e.g. when some NE conducts a switchover) and in this case the counter is not updated.

2G|142004.Description: The sum of Voltage Standing Wave Ratio (VSWR). The counter reports the sum of VSWR value samples taken every 1 minute during the measurement period. Transmitted power and reflected power interferes and forms a standing wave. The VSWR is defined as the ratio of maximum to minimum in this wave. VSWR = (transmitted power + reflected power)/ (transmitted power -reflected power). If the VSWR value is unreliable for the whole period, the value is set to 0xFF. An actual measured VSWR value is reported as multiplied with 10. Unreliable conditions are invalid VSWR alarm, TX low power alarm, VSWR minor alarm or VSWR major alarm. Average value is calculated by dividing the value of this counter by the value of the counter 142005.

2G|150001.Description: The number of TCH assignments on node of CMST cell.
2G|150001.Description in previous release: The number of TCH assignments on node of CMST cell.
2G|150001.Updated: In a case of a new call or re-establishment on node of CMST cell, the counter is updated once the MEASUREMENT RESULT message is received after the ASSIGNMENT COMPLETE the first time on TCH from the BTS. In a case of FACCH call set-up due to SDCCH congestion, the counter is updated, when an ESTABLISH INDICATION message is received on the TCH from the BTS. In case of normal directed retry (inter-cell directed retry), the counter is updated, when a HANDOVER COMPLETE message is received on the TCH from the BTS. In case of na inter-cell TCH-TCH and external TCH - TCH handover, the counter is updated once the MEASUREMENT RESULT message is received after a HANDOVER COMPLETE or an ASSIGNMENT COMPLETE message is received on the TCH from the BTS.

2G|513000.Description: An errored block is a block in which one or more bits have an error. 2G|513023.Network Element Name in previous release: PATH TERMINATION SECTION 3 BACKGROUND BLOCK ERRORS AT THE NEAR END
2G|513023.Description: An errored block in which one or more bits have an error. B3 byte in the HO-POH is used for path termination section error monitoring using Bit Interleaved Parity 8 (BIP-8) code, in an even parity. The BIP-8 is computed over all the bits of the previous virtual container/virtual tributary (VC-12 over VC-3 or VC-12 over VC-4 according to configuration) and is placed in byte B3 of the current frame. In this case the block means virtual container/virtual tributary.

2G|513027.Network Element Name: MULTIPLEX SECTION LINE BACKGROUND BLOCK ERRORS AT THE FAR END
2G|513027.Network Element Name in previous release: MULTIPLEX SECTION LINE BACKGROUND BLOCK ERRORS AT THE FAR END
2G|513027.Description: An errored block is a block in which one or more bits have an error. M1 byte conveys the count of errored blocks, which is calculated by the far end from its receiving blocks by using B2 bytes at multiplexer level. B2 bytes are the bytes allocated for a Multiplex section line error monitoring function, which is Bit Interleaved Parity 24 (BIP-24) code using even parity. The BIP-24 is computed over all bits of the previous STM frame exluding RSOH and is placed in byte B2 of the current frame. In this case the block means STM-1/OC3 frame.
